question: What is the primary site of absorption for most orally administered medications?
explanation: Most oral drugs are absorbed across the mucosal lining of the stomach and small intestine into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why does first-pass metabolism reduce the systemic concentration of oral drugs?

options.A: The liver metabolizes part of the drug before it reaches general circulation
options.B: Intestinal enzymes convert the active drug molecules into inactive water
options.C: Food particles bind to the medication and push it out through the colon
options.D: Gastric acid completely destroys all active chemical ingredients instantly

explanation: Blood from the gut flows directly to the liver via the portal system, where hepatic enzymes break down a portion of the drug. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which clinical situation makes the oral route completely inappropriate for a patient?

options.A: An acute emergency requiring immediate drug action
options.B: A stable chronic high blood pressure condition
options.C: A patient recovering well from minor surgery
options.D: A mild headache that started two hours ago

explanation: Oral medications take time to dissolve and absorb, making them useless when instant therapeutic blood levels are needed. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is a major safety advantage of the oral route compared to intravenous injections?

options.A: It is easier to reverse or intercept an overdose via the GI tract
options.B: It completely bypasses the metabolic filtering action of the liver
options.C: It causes zero irritation to the lining of the digestive system
options.D: It guarantees 100 percent absorption of every administered dose

explanation: The slower absorption window allows healthcare providers time to use interventions like gastric emptying if an error occurs. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why must suspension medications be shaken thoroughly before pouring a dose?

options.A: To cool down the mixture and prevent unpleasant warm tastes
options.B: To dissolve the outer gelatin shell of the suspended drug
options.C: To activate the chemical preservative agents inside the bottle
options.D: To evenly redistribute the settled solid particles in the liquid

explanation: Active drug particles in suspensions settle at the bottom over time, requiring agitation to ensure the patient gets the correct dose. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h3)

question: What happens if a nurse crushes an enteric-coated tablet before administration?

options.A: The patient will find the taste much sweeter and easier to swallow
options.B: Stomach acid will destroy the drug and irritate the gastric lining
options.C: The drug will transform into a liquid syrup inside the medicine cup
options.D: The medication will absorb much faster and work twice as effectively

explanation: Enteric coatings protect drugs from stomach acid and protect the stomach from irritating drugs; crushing ruins this protective barrier. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why should nurses use a calibrated device instead of a kitchen spoon for liquid drugs?

options.A: Kitchen spoons vary greatly in size and do not measure accurate doses
options.B: Calibrated medicine cups chemically neutralize toxic elements in syrups
options.C: Hospital policy strictly forbids touching any utensil from a kitchen
options.D: Standard household spoons react badly with acidic liquid medications

explanation: Household spoons lack standardization, which can easily lead to underdosing or dangerous overdosing of liquid medications. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h4)

question: A nurse is preparing to give morning pills to a stroke patient with left-sided weakness. What is the immediate priority assessment?

options.A: Evaluate the patient's swallowing reflex and gag function
options.B: Ask the family members if the patient slept well last night
options.C: Check the patient's blood pressure using a manual cuff
options.D: Measure the exact abdominal girth with a flexible tape

explanation: Stroke patients often suffer from dysphagia, making a swallow assessment crucial to prevent aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of checking the patient's identification band before giving pills?

options.A: To look up the patient's personal phone number and home address
options.B: To confirm the correct patient receives the prescribed medication
options.C: To check if the patient has paid their hospital admission bills
options.D: To verify the exact hospital room number and bed assignment

explanation: Patient identification prevents administration errors caused by similar names or mistaken bed assignments. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the correct physical position for a patient receiving oral medications?

options.A: Prone position resting flat on the abdomen
options.C: Upright sitting position at a 90-degree angle
options.D: Flat on the back with the head turned to the side

explanation: An upright posture uses gravity to help the pill move down the esophagus and prevents aspiration into the lungs. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why should a nurse never leave medication unattended on a patient's bedside table?

options.A: The patient might forget to take it or the wrong person could ingest it
options.B: The hospital pharmacy will charge extra fees for delayed dosing
options.C: Tablets will dissolve in the air if exposed to room temperature
options.D: Hospital cleaning staff might accidentally throw the medication away

explanation: Leaving drugs unattended violates safety protocols because adherence cannot be verified and visitors or children might ingest them. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is it dangerous to mix a child's crushed medication into their daily milk feed?

options.A: Milk chemically neutralizes the active ingredients in all known drugs
options.B: It can create a permanent aversion to a vital dietary food item
options.C: Children will refuse to drink anything that tastes sweet
options.D: The fat content in milk completely dissolves the pill container

explanation: Mixing drugs in essential foods like milk can cause children to distrust and reject their regular nutritional meals. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h7)

question: What should a nurse do when an unconscious patient has an order for oral medication?

options.A: Mix the tablets in a large cup of water and use a syringe quickly
options.B: Wait until the patient wakes up naturally later in the evening
options.C: Crush the pills and force them past the teeth using a tongue depressor
options.D: Contact the prescriber to discuss an alternative route of administration

explanation: Unconscious patients lack protective airway reflexes, making the oral route unsafe and requiring routes like IV or rectal administration. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h7)

question: When is the correct time for a nurse to document administered medications on the chart?

options.A: Whenever the prescribing doctor asks for a progress report
options.B: Before leaving the medication room to start the ward round
options.C: At the end of the entire eight-hour nursing shift
options.D: Immediately after the patient swallows the medication

explanation: Documentation must happen right after administration to prevent accidental double-dosing by other staff members. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h8)

question: What action is required if a patient vomits five minutes after swallowing a tablet?

options.A: Wait twenty minutes and administer another whole pill quietly
options.B: Assume the drug was fully absorbed and ignore the vomiting event
options.C: Inspect the vomitus, document the occurrence, and notify the prescriber
options.D: Immediately force the patient to swallow a replacement double dose

explanation: Vomiting shortly after ingestion means the drug may not have been absorbed, requiring medical evaluation before re-administering. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h8)
